result.title: Policy Iteration Is Not Strongly Polynomial for Deterministic Markov Decision Processes: The Price of Algorithmic Anarchy
result.summary: We establish an exponential iteration lower bound in the number of states for Howard's policy iteration on deterministic discounted Markov decision processes, with at most two actions per state. This rules out strong polynomiality of Howard's policy iteration when the discount factor is part of the input and yields an exponential separation from the simplex method with Dantzig's pivoting rule, which is proved to be strongly polynomial on this class. Even when each reward is restricted to logarithmic bit length, we obtain a stretched-exponential iteration lower bound. The gap between Howard's decentralized and simultaneous selfish improvements and Dantzig's coordinated selection of a single action with the largest gain across all states reveals a ``price'' of algorithmic anarchy.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文证明 Howard 策略迭代在确定性折扣 MDP（每状态至多两个动作）上存在状态数的指数迭代下界，从而否定其在折扣因子计入输入时的强多项式性，并与 Dantzig 单纯形法形成指数分离，借此讨论「算法无政府」的代价。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关联，但策略迭代的收敛下界与「分散式改动 vs 全局协调」的对比，可能为 latent 推理中迭代状态更新的步数代价、停止决策与资源分配提供反面参照，可供核查。
